title: Field signal matrix for model cost & resilience in niche verticals
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Create a reproducible field-signal matrix and investigative playbook to evaluate model cost-resilience tradeoffs for niche verticals (legal, healthcare transcription, regional finance). This ticket captures the research plan, competitive signal collection approach, measurement buckets, and recommended operational triggers for model fallback and procurement. Goal: produce a one-page provisioning rubric + a 10-scenario runbook for the Growth/PM/SRE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix populated with at least 12 models (open & commercial) across 3 verticals and annotated with latency/cost/quality signals
Operational triggers defined for fallback policy (latency spike, cost delta, availability loss) with concrete thresholds
Dashboard prototype link with synthetic workload slices and cost/resilience visualizations
Stakeholder review (+PM, Infra SRE, Solutions Eng) completed and signoff recorded
tasks: Assemble initial model list and provenance notes (open-source weights, hosted vendors)
Define measurement slices: average tokens/req, p95 latency, token cost delta, top-K accuracy proxy
Run synthetic workloads for 3 vertical prompts and capture metrics
Draft fallback trigger thresholds and validate with SRE on capacity implications
Write provisioning rubric and embed sample rollout configs for Dedicated vs Hosted
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Growth, SRE, and Solutions Eng. Agreed verticals (legal summarization, telemedicine notes, APAC finance feed). Action: Aisha to compile model candidate list.
2026-02-27: Compiled 18 candidate models (mix of open quantized variants and hosted offerings). Uploaded raw provenance to Drive.
2026-03-03: Synthetic workload test harness PR opened (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/probes/pull/158). ENG requested rate-limit awareness in harness.
2026-03-07: First run completed — notable finding: two small open quantized models show 30% cost advantage but degrade on long-context legal transcripts. Documented in notes.
2026-03-10: Design review with PM lead; recommended adding a customer-impact weight to the matrix. Updated acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12: SRE feedback: fallback policy must include a cache-warmup step to avoid cold-start latency spikes. Added to tasks and runbook.
2026-03-15: Draft matrix shared with Solutions Eng. Next: stakeholder signoff and dashboard prototype refinement due 2026-03-22.
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Choose vertical-first approach (test realistic prompts) over generic microbenchmarks — rationale: real signal fidelity
2026-03-03: Include both open quantized variants and hosted endpoints in matrix — rationale: procurement and fallback decisions require cross-environment comparability
2026-03-12: Require cache-warmup step on fallback to Dedicated capacity — rationale: avoid user-visible latency regressions during model switch
notes: Primary novelty: combine cost delta with operational friction (cache warmup time, quantization regression risk) and assign a weighted score per vertical. Use this to drive canary->canary-fallback sequences in Redwood Console rollouts.
estimate_rationale: 5 points: two weeks of cross-team testing, dashboard prototype, and write-up; relies on SRE time for validation
impact_summary: Enables PM and SRE to make procurement decisions with quantified tradeoffs and automated triggers; reduces unplanned failovers and cost surprises for mid-market customers
mitigations: If model-run metrics vary by >15% between synthetic and field traffic, schedule a 3-day field validation window before enforced rollout
Add a manual override in rollout UI for high-impact accounts during fallback tests
Log fallback events to a dedicated audit stream for postmortem analysis
